title: Shipping Production-Ready RAG Applications
excerpt: Everything we learned building retrieval-augmented AI features that users actually trust.
metaDescription: A field guide to shipping production-ready RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) apps: chunking, retrieval quality, evaluation and guardrails.
author: Wynex Editorial
content:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is the fastest path to an AI feature that knows your business. But the gap between a weekend demo and a product users trust is wide. Here is what actually matters when you take RAG to production.

## Retrieval quality is the whole game

Most "the model is hallucinating" problems are really retrieval problems — the model never saw the right context. Invest here first.

### Chunk with intent

Don't split documents on a fixed character count. Chunk on semantic boundaries — headings, sections, list items — so each chunk is a self-contained idea. Add a little overlap so context isn't severed mid-thought.

### Enrich your embeddings

Prepend each chunk with its document title and section path before embedding. This small change dramatically improves retrieval for short, ambiguous chunks.

### Hybrid search beats pure vectors

Combine dense vector search with keyword (BM25) search. Vectors capture meaning; keywords catch exact identifiers, error codes and product names that embeddings often blur.

## Evaluate before you ship

Build a small golden set of real questions with known-good answers. Score retrieval (did we fetch the right chunks?) and generation (was the answer correct and grounded?) separately. Without evaluation you are flying blind — a prompt tweak that helps one case silently breaks five others.

## Guardrails users can trust

- **Cite sources.** Show which documents an answer came from. Citations turn a black box into a tool people trust.
- **Say "I don't know."** Instruct the model to refuse when retrieval returns nothing relevant, rather than inventing an answer.
- **Keep a human in the loop** for high-stakes actions, and log everything for review.

## Operate it like software

RAG systems drift as your documents change. Monitor retrieval hit-rate, track answer quality on your golden set, and re-index on a schedule. Treat prompts and chunking configs as versioned artifacts, not magic strings. To keep repeated questions fast and cheap at scale, layer in [semantic caching for LLM responses](/blog/implementing-semantic-caching-for-llm-applications), and if you serve multiple customers from one index, enforce strict [tenant isolation at the database layer](/blog/multi-tenant-postgres-row-level-security-guide) so retrieval never crosses account boundaries.

## The takeaway

Great RAG is 20% model and 80% engineering discipline — clean retrieval, honest evaluation, and guardrails that make the system trustworthy. Get those right and you ship an AI feature people genuinely rely on.
